key_insight: Grad Detect uses a single forward-backward pass to read layer-wise gradient patterns, which reveal when an LLM is likely hallucinating better than output confidence alone.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical, inference-time reliability check that can improve deployment safety for LLMs in high-stakes Q&A and abstention settings.
method: Compute gradients during inference from one forward-backward pass.
Use layer-wise gradient structure as a hallucination signal.
Focus on the final five layers, which contain most of the discriminative information.
evidence_signal: Across several Q&A benchmarks and eleven models from four architectural families, the method consistently outperforms confidence-based and sampling-based baselines, with the final five layers carrying over 97% of the useful signal.
watch_item: Because it requires backward-pass computation at inference, runtime and memory overhead may limit use in latency-sensitive deployments.
paper_title: Grad Detect: Gradient-Based Hallucination Detection in LLMs
